name: PlaceHolder 1
text: Introduction

name: PlaceHolder 2
text:
Project overview: CampusAI is an academic helpdesk for Aditya University. It interprets student questions and retrieves curriculum evidence with document and page references.
Application domain: Natural Language Processing and Information Retrieval for B.Tech Curriculum 2024, Version 3.0, across eight engineering departments.
Student needs: Students can ask about course codes, credits, semester subjects, syllabus units, prerequisites, and academic regulations.
Project objective: Combine intent classification, exact database lookup, and hybrid document retrieval to make academic answers easier to find and verify.
Sources: backend/config.py, backend/rag/generator.py, data/structured/resource_catalog.json. Scope: B.Tech Curriculum 2024 Version 3.0.

name: PlaceHolder 1
text: Problem Definition

name: PlaceHolder 2
text:
Existing problem: Academic information spans eight curriculum PDFs containing 6,502 pages. Students must identify the correct department, semester, and source page.
Search difficulties: Abbreviations, paraphrases, and Telugu-English queries can obscure intent. Similar course names also require department context.
Risk of incorrect answers: Wrong credits, prerequisites, or semester details can mislead academic planning. A fluent answer alone does not establish accuracy.
Affected users: Students seeking academic guidance and staff who repeatedly answer curriculum questions.
Required improvement: Route factual questions to structured records and support descriptive answers with traceable evidence, clarification, or abstention.
Sources: data/manifests/source_quality_report.json, backend/nlp/entity_extractor.py, backend/nlp/coreference.py. Corpus counts are manifest values.

name: PlaceHolder 1
text: Proposed Solution

name: PlaceHolder 2
text:
Query understanding: Identify language, normalize academic terms, predict one of 30 intents, and extract course, department, semester, and unit entities.
Exact academic facts: Use SQL retrieval for structured details such as course codes, credits, and semester offerings.
Syllabus and topic search: Combine BM25 keyword retrieval with dense semantic search, fuse rankings with RRF, and rerank candidate passages.
Evidence-based responses: Generate answers from retrieved content, attach document and page references, and request clarification when the query is ambiguous.
Student application: A React and TypeScript interface connects to FastAPI for chat, course exploration, semester views, comparisons, and source viewing.

Sources: backend/nlp/intent_classifier.py, scripts/train_intent_model.py, backend/rag/retriever.py, backend/rag/generator.py, frontend/src. Capabilities describe implemented components, not guarantees of answer correctness.

name: PlaceHolder 1
text: Data Used

name: PlaceHolder 2
text:
Official source corpus: Eight Aditya University B.Tech Curriculum 2024 PDFs, Version 3.0, covering 6,502 pages.
Department coverage: CSE, CSE-DS, IT, ECE, EEE, Civil Engineering, Mining Engineering, and Petroleum Technology.
Structured academic catalog: 569 registered courses, 583 syllabus units, and 1,273 textbook references.
Intent dataset: 1,201 labeled queries across 30 classes. Fields include query, intent, domain, language, course, department, semester, and unit.
Training and evaluation: A stratified 80/20 split gives 960 training and 241 test queries. Separate stratified five-fold cross-validation estimates model stability.
Data formats: PDF source documents, a CSV query dataset, JSON metadata and indices, and a relational academic database.

Sources: data/manifests/source_quality_report.json (8 PDFs, 6,502 pages), data/structured/resource_catalog.json (catalog counts), data/aditya_university_queries.csv (1,201 rows, 30 intents), scripts/train_intent_model.py (stratified 20% test split, random seed 42), reports/classification_report.txt (241 test samples). The remaining 960 queries form the training split. Cross-validation runs separately over the full dataset. Counts replace the older synthetic CampusFAQ-50K figures in the template.

name: PlaceHolder 1
text: Modules

name: PlaceHolder 2
text:
Text Preprocessing and Query Understanding
Normalize case, punctuation, and whitespace while preserving course codes, academic acronyms, and Telugu text. Extract entities and handle follow-up or multi-intent questions.
Intent Classification
Combine word and character TF-IDF features with calibrated Linear SVM, Logistic Regression, and Complement Naive Bayes. Confidence and alternative intents support query routing.
Retrieval, Grounding, and Application
Retrieve exact facts through SQL and descriptive evidence through hybrid search. The RAG layer adds citations, while the web app provides chat, course exploration, comparisons, and PDF source viewing.

Sources: backend/nlp/preprocessing.py, scripts/train_intent_model.py, backend/nlp/intent_classifier.py, backend/rag/retriever.py, backend/rag/generator.py, frontend/src. Stopword removal defaults to disabled. Lemmatization is conditional on available NLTK resources.
NLP Query Understanding
1. Language and text normalization

Recognize English, Telugu, or mixed queries. Normalize case, punctuation, and whitespace while preserving course codes and academic abbreviations. Lemmatization is optional when language resources are available.
2. Academic entity extraction
Identify the course, department, semester, and unit independently of intent. For “Explain Unit 3 of Operating Systems in CSE,” the entities specify which syllabus content to retrieve.
3. Context and ambiguity handling
Use earlier turns to interpret follow-up questions. Ask for clarification when an abbreviation has multiple meanings, and decompose requests that ask for more than one type of academic information.

Sources: backend/nlp/preprocessing.py, backend/nlp/normalizer.py, backend/nlp/entity_extractor.py, backend/nlp/coreference.py, backend/nlp/multi_intent.py. Example illustrates parsing and does not assert a new model prediction.
TF-IDF Feature Extraction
Word features: phrases of one to three words
Word n-grams preserve expressions such as “course credits” and “semester total credits.” TF-IDF reduces the influence of frequent terms and gives more weight to terms that distinguish queries.
Character features: sequences of two to five characters
Character n-grams capture fragments within word boundaries. They provide additional signals for spelling variations and related word forms when exact full-word matches differ.
FeatureUnion: one input for all classifiers
The pipeline concatenates word and character TF-IDF vectors. Sublinear term frequency reduces the effect of repeated terms. All three classifiers receive this same sparse feature representation.

Sources: scripts/train_intent_model.py and https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.feature_extraction.text.TfidfVectorizer.html. The character analyzer is char_wb; sublinear_tf=True. This is feature extraction for intent classification, separate from dense retrieval embeddings.
Linear SVM Classifier
How it classifies a query
Linear SVM learns separating boundaries between intent classes in TF-IDF feature space. Its margin-based objective balances class separation against training errors.
Why calibration is required
LinearSVC produces decision scores rather than native probabilities. Three-fold probability calibration converts these scores into estimates that can participate in soft voting.
CampusAI configuration and role
The project uses C = 1.5, squared-hinge loss, and L2 regularization. The calibrated SVM receives two of the ensemble’s five weight units. Its standalone accuracy has not been separately reported.

Sources: scripts/train_intent_model.py; https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/calibration and https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.calibration.CalibratedClassifierCV.html. LinearSVC C=1.5, squared_hinge loss, L2 penalty; CalibratedClassifierCV cv=3. No individual SVM benchmark is reported.
Logistic Regression and NB
Logistic Regression
Learns a weighted relationship between TF-IDF features and each intent. It produces class probabilities directly for the ensemble.
Balanced class weights give rarer classes more influence during training. The project uses C = 5.0, the lbfgs solver, and up to 1,000 iterations.
Voting weight: 2
Complement Naive Bayes
Uses feature statistics from the other classes to score an intent. It offers a different statistical approach to sparse text classification.
Smoothing reduces the effect of unseen features. CampusAI sets alpha = 0.3 and enables weight normalization with norm = True.
Voting weight: 1

Sources: scripts/train_intent_model.py; https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.linear_model.LogisticRegression.html; https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.naive_bayes.ComplementNB.html. LR uses C=5, lbfgs, max_iter=1000, class_weight=balanced. ComplementNB uses alpha=0.3 and norm=True. No standalone comparative scores are available.
Soft-Voting Ensemble
Weighted probability combination
For each intent, the ensemble combines calibrated SVM, Logistic Regression, and Complement Naive Bayes probabilities. The final intent has the highest combined score.
Voting rule
Combined score = (2 × SVM probability + 2 × LR probability + NB probability) / 5. The weights are project settings, not the result of a reported model-comparison study.
Illustrative calculation
If the three probabilities for course_credits are 0.80, 0.70, and 0.60, its combined score is 0.72. This explains the voting rule; it is not a measured prediction.

Sources: scripts/train_intent_model.py; https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.ensemble.VotingClassifier.html. The arithmetic illustration is hypothetical and not an observed model output. Confidence is not a probability of end-to-end answer correctness.
The 30 Intent Classes
Families group the existing labels for explanation. The classifier predicts one of the 30 individual intents.

Source: reports/model_metrics.json classes array. The six families below are explanatory groupings for the presentation, not a new learned hierarchy. All 30 class labels are represented in readable form.
Hybrid Retrieval Algorithms
BM25: match specific academic terms
Sparse retrieval scores keyword relevance using term frequency, inverse document frequency, and document length. Exact course names and codes provide useful lexical signals.
MiniLM: match semantic meaning
all-MiniLM-L6-v2 maps queries and document chunks to 384-dimensional vectors. Cosine similarity ranks passages by vector similarity, helping match related wording.
Reciprocal Rank Fusion: combine both lists
RRF adds each passage’s contribution from its rank in each result list: weight / (60 + rank). A passage appearing near the top of both lists receives a stronger combined score.

Sources: backend/rag/retriever.py, backend/rag/embeddings.py, data/structured/resource_catalog.json. reciprocal_rank_fusion uses k=60 and rank positions starting at 1. The embedding model and fallback behavior depend on runtime availability.
Reranking and Grounding
Cross-encoder reranking
The reranker scores each query and candidate passage together, then selects the highest-ranked evidence. CampusAI uses a MiniLM cross-encoder with a lexical fallback if the model is unavailable.
Exact lookup and answer generation
Structured questions use SQL academic records. Descriptive questions use retrieved passages as context for the answer generator. This separates factual lookup from free-text synthesis.
Citation checks and response boundaries

Checks validate source identifiers, page numbers, and mentioned course codes. Missing evidence can trigger abstention or clarification. These checks improve traceability but do not prove every answer claim is correct.

Sources: backend/rag/reranker.py, backend/rag/citation_verifier.py, backend/rag/prompt_builder.py, backend/rag/generator.py, backend/database/sql_retriever.py. CitationVerifier checks document IDs, positive page numbers, and mentioned course codes; it does not prove every claim is entailed by a source. Reranker uses lexical fallback if model loading or inference fails.

The student asks for Operating Systems credits in CSE.

Course details, a document ID, and a page reference accompany the answer.
Recorded application demo. The source reference supports inspection of the returned academic details.

Verification workflow
A student can inspect the curriculum table and compare the cited course record with the answer.
Recorded application demo. Page references make source checking possible; users should verify disputed details.

Results: Overall Performance
1,201 labeled queries    30 intents    960 train / 241 test
Saved evaluation from 22 October 2026. Scores describe intent classification on the project dataset.

Sources: reports/model_metrics.json, saved 2026-10-22 08:09:45 UTC; reports/classification_report.txt; scripts/train_intent_model.py. 1,201 samples, 960 train, 241 test, stratified split, seed 42. 232/241 = 96.26556%, 239/241 = 99.17012%, inferred integer counts agree with rounded reported scores. CV runs independently over the full dataset. Retrieval constants from backend/evaluation/benchmark_runner.py are excluded.
Results: Performance by Intent
Small class sizes limit confidence. A separate student-query test set is needed to assess real-world performance.

name: PlaceHolder 1
text: Conclusion and Future Scope

name: PlaceHolder 2
text:
Conclusion
CampusAI integrates NLP query understanding, structured academic lookup, and hybrid evidence retrieval for eight departments. The latest intent classifier reaches 96.27% accuracy on the held-out project test set.
Current Limitations
Coverage centres on Curriculum 2024, Version 3.0. The test set is small for some intents, and out-of-scope detection has an F1 score of 0.40. Retrieval relevance and answer correctness need independent evaluation.
Future Scope
Collect student queries across languages, strengthen low-performing intents, and evaluate retrieval against human relevance labels. Expand verified curriculum coverage and connect approved live academic notices.

Sources: reports/classification_report.txt (out_of_scope F1 0.4000 with support 3; admission_information F1 0.5714 with support 4), docs/LIMITATIONS.md, backend/evaluation/benchmark_runner.py. Future work is proposed work. The project dataset may not represent real student query distributions, and the current split is not an independently collected student evaluation.
